title: Key Evaluation of a Relativistic Quantum Key Distribution Over a Turbulent Free-space Optical Channel
abstract: We investigate the performance of relativistic quantum key distribution (RQKD) over turbulent free-space optical channels for both single-photon and coherent-state implementations. A theoretical model is developed to describe the effect of atmospheric turbulence on interferometric visibility and secret-key generation by incorporating turbulence-induced phase fluctuations into the key-rate analysis. Numerical simulations are performed under realistic channel conditions to evaluate the achievable communication distance and secret-key rate. The results show that atmospheric turbulence degrades the protocol performance by reducing interference visibility, with the severity of the degradation determined by the ratio between the interferometer-arm separation $r$ (or temporal separation of signal and reference states $ΔT$) and Fried's parameter. The single-photon protocol remains operational over all investigated turbulence regimes, whereas the coherent-state implementation exhibits a critical dependence on the interferometer geometry (especially on $ΔT$), leading to a threshold beyond which secure key generation is no longer possible. These findings quantify the impact of atmospheric turbulence on relativistic quantum key distribution and provide practical guidelines for the design and optimization of free-space RQKD systems.
summary: This work quantifies the impact of atmospheric turbulence on Relativistic Quantum Key Distribution (RQKD) over free-space optical links. By modeling phase fluctuations, the authors show that while single-photon protocols are robust, coherent-state implementations face a critical threshold due to turbulence. The findings provide essential guidelines for designing reliable quantum communication systems in atmospheric channels.
main_problem: The paper evaluates the performance of Relativistic Quantum Key Distribution (RQKD) when transmitted over a turbulent Free-space Optical (FSO) channel.
main_result: Atmospheric turbulence degrades key rate by reducing interference visibility; the single-photon protocol remains robust, while the coherent-state implementation fails beyond a critical interferometer geometry.
method: A theoretical model incorporating turbulence-induced phase fluctuations is developed, followed by numerical simulations to analyze the achievable secret-key rate.
model_or_system: The system involves interferometric setups for both single-photon and weak coherent-state RQKD protocols transmitted through a turbulent FSO channel.
key_observables: Secret-key rate, interference visibility, Quantum Bit Error Rate (QBER).
important_parameters: Interferometer-arm separation ($r$ or $\Delta T$), Fried's parameter, turbulence variance ($\sigma^2_\phi$), and channel transmissivity ($\eta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes independent fluctuations for phase components and uses asymptotic limits for key rate calculations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the interferometric setups for both single-photon and coherent-state RQKD, along with spacetime diagrams showing the time evolution of the quantum states.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical model, analyzes the key rate expressions for both single-photon and coherent-state regimes, derives the impact of turbulence on detection probability and error rates, and concludes with practical guidelines.
why_interesting: It directly addresses the practical limitations of quantum communication protocols in realistic atmospheric environments, which is crucial for quantum optics and quantum networking research.
